identity.name: Operational Zone of the Alpine Foothills
identity.wikipedia: Operational Zone of the Alpine Foothills

land.text: 'the provinces of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento'; the page says the Germans restored the 1919 provincial borders, plus Belluno

predecessors.note: The provinces of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento, occupied by the Wehrmacht two days after the armistice with Italy was proclaimed.

land.text: 'given back to Italy only in 1947 when it had become a Republic'; Bolzano was first placed under military occupation

successors.note: The page says the land came back in 1947; the Kingdom of Italy dossier covers 1945-1946 with an Allied administration of the region.

capitals.name: Bolzano (Bozen)
capitals.note: 'The capital of the zone was Bolzano.' The infobox gives 'Bozen'.

rulers.name: Franz Hofer
rulers.title: High Commissioner
rulers.note: Infobox '1943–1945: Franz Hofer'; 'OZAV was administered by High Commissioner Franz Hofer'. Hofer wanted the zone merged into his Gau; Hitler declined, the page says, to show consideration for Mussolini.

correction.text: 'the provinces of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento'; the page says the Germans restored the 1919 provincial borders, plus Belluno

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no shape for the zone. The page gives no area or population (page silent); the three provinces resolve to about 16,000 km2. The page says the Germans restored the 1919 provincial borders, plus Belluno, so the modern Bozen and Trento boundaries are the best name; it is separate from the Italian Social Republic (the RSI page's footnote disagrees).

region.text: 'the provinces of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento'; the page says the Germans restored the 1919 provincial borders, plus Belluno

ledger.note: 10 September 1943: the Wehrmacht sets up the Operational Zone of the Alpine Foothills. 'OZAV was established on 10 September 1943 by the occupying German Wehrmacht', two days after the armistice with Italy was proclaimed; 'It comprised the provinces of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento.'

region.text: the zone under High Commissioner Franz Hofer, administered as part of the Reichsgau Tirol-Vorarlberg

ledger.note: 10 September 1943: the zone is administered with the Reichsgau Tirol-Vorarlberg. 'The zone was administered as part of the Reichsgau of Tirol-Vorarlberg'; Hofer wanted it merged into his Gau but it was not, because Hitler wanted to show consideration for Mussolini.

region.text: 'the provinces of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento'; the page says the Germans restored the 1919 provincial borders, plus Belluno

ledger.note: 3 May 1945: German rule collapses. '41 people killed at Bolzano on 3 May 1945, when Wehrmacht and SS units fired on civilians'; 11 killed in Merano on 30 April 1945; 'After the German surrender in Italy'. The page gives no day for the end of German rule.

region.text: 'the provinces of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento'; the page says the Germans restored the 1919 provincial borders, plus Belluno

ledger.note: May 1945: the Operational Zone of the Alpine Foothills ends. Infobox 'Disestablishment: 1945'. The page does not describe the Allied entry; the land was 'given back to Italy only in 1947 when it had become a Republic'.

certainty.note: The zone follows the provincial borders of Belluno, Bolzano and Trento (the page says the Germans restored the 1919 provincial borders, plus Belluno).

sources.title: Operational Zone of the Alpine Foothills
sources.note: Establishment 10 September 1943, three provinces, Bolzano capital, Franz Hofer, Reichsgau Tirol-Vorarlberg, end 1945, return to Italy 1947. No area.

sources.title: Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral
sources.note: Twin zone; both separate from the Italian Social Republic.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the zone. The RSI page footnote ('still formally part of the RSI') and the zone pages ('separate') disagree; the italian-social-republic shape leaves the zone out. The page has no area, no formal end day (3 May 1945 is from the Bolzano killings), and does not describe the Allied entry or the military occupation of 1945-1947. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none.
